x: Although missing the medals Steve Williams took the handicap prize with the most promising run of the day. New to the sport this winter but looking every inch a runner, he is sure to trouble the best in Belgrave by this time next year.

Steve Williams has had an interesting first track season. The Jubilee Relay saw him miss his take-over, sprint 200 metres to grab the baton and then commence to run his mile whilst divesting himself of most of his tracksuit.

Steve Williams was the unfortunate one - he hadn't stripped off ready to take stage 14 for the A team and his time represents some kind of record for running to the change-over point and doing a striptease while running the first 2 laps.

Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
Steve Williams leads a group that includes a National cross country champion on numerous occasions - Pam Davies.
Alan Painter was the deserving handicap winner but Steve Williams must also get a mention, finishing as he did cut, bruised and muddied from a very heavy fall on the horseride.
Our scoring men, mostly "the old gang" were anchored by Steve Williams with Peter Hardwick and Simon Holmes hot on his heels - these three are soon going to worry our established seniors.
Steve Williams, finishing a Rosenheim League 800m at Tooting.

Leo Coy's training started to pay off as he finished 6th ahead of newcomer (!) Steve Williams having his first race for two months. The handicapper was seen surveying the scene with pleasure (glad he wasn't running perhaps!) and even pacing Peter Hardwick over the last lap while retrieving the flags!!

Tony Binda was forced to stop and walk on the second lap with bad cramp in the stomach and Steve Williams, after a promising return in the '10', was forced to retire with the same diaphragm trouble that has dogged him since the summer.

U.S.sprint star Steve Williams' 100 metre victory looked very impressive. How nice it was, then, to have our own Ernest Obeng present, who had run Williams to within hundredths of a second a few short months previously.
Also over 800 metres, Nick Kirmatzis just edged Steve Williams, 2:01.5 to 2:01.8 - both seasonal bests. Mark Shippen took his 1980 best a little higher by vaulting 4.20.
As Steve Williams remarked - "This was Oliver's finest win to date". Several ladies competed in this years race, fastest of whom was new member Jill Davies.

In Steve Williams' 5¾mile Road Run Table the name of Alan Jerman occurs next to last with a date of Mar. 40. With the maxim of "Lest we forget" in mind I would mention that Alan Jerman was unfortunately Belgrave Harriers' first fatality in World War II.
Notes written by Steve Williams in the '80s have played their part, as too have helpful comments from Gordon Doubleday and additional information from Snowy Brooks and Laurie O'Hara.
Many thanks in particular to Peter Matthews, Jacinta Moore, Steve Williams, Dave Sharpe, Charlie Dickinson, Helen Maskrey, Gary Staines and Derek Jones.

Steve Williams writes from deepest Sussex. A true statistician, the article about the Christmas Paalauf in our last issue prompted him to inform us that he has now, on his own, achieved the combined ages of John Gladwin and himself when they won the event (and it seems like yesterday).
